claims.title: Foundation of the Mossi states
claims.summary: Tradition attributes the Mossi kingdoms of Tenkodogo, Ouagadougou and Yatenga to the line of Ouédraogo, son of the princess Yennenga; the dating is uncertain and some accounts place the origins earlier.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1450-foundation-of-the-mossi-states, claim TL:BFA:event:1450:foundation-of-the-mossi-states, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Songhai campaigns against the Mossi
claims.summary: The Songhai emperor Askia Muhammad I campaigns against the non-Muslim Mossi, defeating Mossi of Yatenga but failing to subdue the kingdoms, which retain their religion and independence.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1498-songhai-campaigns-against-the-mossi, claim TL:BFA:event:1498:songhai-campaigns-against-the-mossi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Yatenga becomes independent of Ouagadougou
claims.summary: As central authority weakens, the kingdom of Yatenga, with its capital at Ouahigouya, breaks free of Ouagadougou's overlordship.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1700-yatenga-becomes-independent-of-ouagadougou, claim TL:BFA:event:1700:yatenga-becomes-independent-of-ouagadougou, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Loropéni's gold-trade fortresses flourish
claims.summary: The stone enclosures of the Lobi country, including Loropéni, reach their height as the trans-Saharan gold trade peaks; the settlements are linked to the Lohron and Kulango peoples.

sources.label: Ruins of Loropéni — World Heritage Centre

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1400-loropeni-s-gold-trade-fortresses-flourish, claim TL:BFA:event:1400:loropeni-s-gold-trade-fortresses-flourish, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Loropéni settlement abandoned
claims.summary: The fortified settlement at Loropéni is abandoned, for reasons still debated by archaeologists.

sources.label: Ruins of Loropéni — World Heritage Centre

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1820-loropeni-settlement-abandoned, claim TL:BFA:event:1820:loropeni-settlement-abandoned, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Loropéni inscribed by UNESCO
claims.summary: The Ruins of Loropéni are added to the UNESCO World Heritage List, becoming Burkina Faso's first such site.

sources.label: Ruins of Loropéni — World Heritage Centre
13 new sites added to UNESCO's World Heritage List (2009)

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-2009-loropeni-inscribed-by-unesco, claim TL:BFA:event:2009:loropeni-inscribed-by-unesco, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: French conquest of the Mossi
claims.summary: France claims the Volta region and occupies Ouagadougou; Mossi resistance collapses and the Mogho Naba Wobgo goes into exile.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1896-french-conquest-of-the-mossi, claim TL:BFA:event:1896:french-conquest-of-the-mossi, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Colony of Upper Volta created
claims.summary: France establishes the separate colony of Upper Volta (Haute-Volta) within French West Africa.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1919-colony-of-upper-volta-created, claim TL:BFA:event:1919:colony-of-upper-volta-created, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Upper Volta partitioned
claims.summary: The colony is dismembered for economic reasons and divided among Côte d'Ivoire, French Sudan and Niger.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1932-upper-volta-partitioned, claim TL:BFA:event:1932:upper-volta-partitioned, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Upper Volta reconstituted
claims.summary: After the war and Mossi pressure, Upper Volta is re-established within its former boundaries as a French West African territory.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1947-upper-volta-reconstituted, claim TL:BFA:event:1947:upper-volta-reconstituted, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Independence of Upper Volta
claims.summary: Upper Volta gains full independence from France; Maurice Yaméogo becomes its first president.

sources.label: List of heads of state of Burkina Faso

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1960-independence-of-upper-volta, claim TL:BFA:event:1960:independence-of-upper-volta, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Fall of Yaméogo; Lamizana takes power
claims.summary: A popular revolt against austerity forces President Yaméogo to resign; Lieutenant Colonel Sangoulé Lamizana leads the army into government.

sources.label: Upper Volta Coup Leads to Military Government

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1966-fall-of-yameogo-lamizana-takes-power, claim TL:BFA:event:1966:fall-of-yameogo-lamizana-takes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coup brings Saye Zerbo to power
claims.summary: Colonel Saye Zerbo overthrows Lamizana, continuing the pattern of military seizures of power.

sources.label: List of heads of state of Burkina Faso

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1980-coup-brings-saye-zerbo-to-power, claim TL:BFA:event:1980:coup-brings-saye-zerbo-to-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo takes over
claims.summary: A further coup ousts Zerbo and installs Major Jean-Baptiste Ouédraogo, in whose government radical young officers, including Thomas Sankara, gain influence.

sources.label: List of heads of state of Burkina Faso

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1982-jean-baptiste-ouedraogo-takes-over, claim TL:BFA:event:1982:jean-baptiste-ouedraogo-takes-over, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Sankara seizes power
claims.summary: Captain Thomas Sankara comes to power in a coup, beginning a radical revolution oriented toward self-reliance and the rural poor.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1983-sankara-seizes-power, claim TL:BFA:event:1983:sankara-seizes-power, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Upper Volta renamed Burkina Faso
claims.summary: On the first anniversary of the revolution, the country is renamed Burkina Faso — 'land of upright (honest) people' — with a new flag and anthem.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1984-upper-volta-renamed-burkina-faso, claim TL:BFA:event:1984:upper-volta-renamed-burkina-faso, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Agacher Strip war with Mali
claims.summary: A brief border conflict, the 'Christmas War', is fought with Mali over the mineral-rich Agacher Strip before regional mediation ends it.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1985-agacher-strip-war-with-mali, claim TL:BFA:event:1985:agacher-strip-war-with-mali, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Assassination of Thomas Sankara
claims.summary: Sankara and twelve others are killed in a coup led by his comrade Blaise Compaoré, who takes the presidency.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1987-assassination-of-thomas-sankara, claim TL:BFA:event:1987:assassination-of-thomas-sankara, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Murder of Norbert Zongo
claims.summary: The investigative journalist Norbert Zongo is killed, a case that becomes a symbol of repression under Compaoré and triggers mass protests.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-1998-murder-of-norbert-zongo, claim TL:BFA:event:1998:murder-of-norbert-zongo, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Popular uprising ousts Compaoré
claims.summary: Protests against Compaoré's bid to extend his rule culminate in the storming of the National Assembly; he resigns after 27 years and flees to Côte d'Ivoire.
claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-2014-popular-uprising-ousts-compaore, claim TL:BFA:event:2014:popular-uprising-ousts-compaore, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Jihadist insurgency spreads to Burkina Faso
claims.summary: Sahelian jihadist groups linked to al-Qaeda and the Islamic State, alongside the homegrown Ansarul Islam, escalate attacks, killing thousands and displacing more than a million people.

sources.label: The Shifting Front of Militant Islamist Violence in the Sahel

claims.citation: Terralore, "The Chronicle of Burkina Faso: From the Mossi kingdoms to the land of upright people", terralore.co/country/BFA/chronicle#ev-2015-jihadist-insurgency-spreads-to-burkina-faso, claim TL:BFA:event:2015:jihadist-insurgency-spreads-to-burkina-faso, retrieved <YYYY-MM-DD>.

claims.title: Coup ousts President Kaboré
claims.summary: Citing the government's failure to halt the insurgency, the military under Lieutenant Colonel Paul-Henri Damiba removes elected president Roch Marc Christian Kaboré.

sources.label: Military Coups, Jihadism and Insecurity in the Central Sahel
sources.publisher: OECD / Sahel and West Africa Club

claims.title: Second 2022 coup brings Ibrahim Traoré to power
claims.summary: Captain Ibrahim Traoré overthrows Damiba in a second coup, becoming transitional leader as jihadist violence continues to spread.

sources.label: Military Coups, Jihadism and Insecurity in the Central Sahel
sources.publisher: OECD / Sahel and West Africa Club
